tone_statements.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2008. Aspects du bongili de la Sangha-Likouala, suivis de l'esquisse du parler énga de Mampoko, Lulonga. (ILCAA Language Monograph Series.) Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. xii+107 pp. DOI 10.15026/85693.
tone_statements.quote: 1.2.4 Tons et syllabes INVENTAIRE DES TONS Il existe, comme on s’en est deja apergu, deux tons de base, simples (bas et haut) et deux tons doubles (descendant et montant). Ces derniers trouvent presque tous leur origine dans la perte d’une consonne intervocalique en diachronie (41b). Avec les tons simples toutes les combinaisons dans les themes nominaux et adjectifs sont permises : HH, HB, BB, BH. … VALEUR DES TONS Les tons ont une valeur lexicale et grammaticale. … Contraction tonale. … Les différentes possibilités sont les suivantes : °H+H > H, °H+B > D, °B+B > B, °B+H > M.
tone_statements.translation: 1.2.4 Tones and syllables. TONE INVENTORY. There are, as already noticed, two basic, simple tones (low and high) and two double tones (falling and rising). The latter almost all originate in the diachronic loss of an intervocalic consonant (41b). With the simple tones all combinations are permitted in nominal and adjectival stems: HH, HL, LL, LH. … VALUE OF THE TONES. The tones have lexical and grammatical value. … Tonal contraction. … The possibilities are: H+H > H, H+L > Falling, L+L > L, L+H > Rising.

tone_statements.citation: Dictionnaire Bongili (Bongili-French online dictionary, with an 'Introduction' overview page). n.d. Webonary.org, SIL International.https://www.webonary.org/bongili/; companion Android app 'Bongili Dictionary' (Google Play id org.sil.bui).
tone_statements.quote: In this dictionary, homographs are indicated by a numerical index (1, 2, 3, …). However, the difference in tones is indicated in the phonetic transcription. [...] Example : shango 1 [ʃáŋgó]: father shango 2 [ʃaŋgo]: new [...] In the phonetic transcription the tones are indicated: the high tone by an acute accent on a vowel and the low tone is not marked. Nevertheless, the tone is not marked on the vowel of the prefix, nor on the final vowel of the verbs, because the tone on these vowels is variable according to the context of the sentence. Examples: ekokolo [ekókóló]: shell, bark boshango [boʃáŋgó]: paternal side, paternity

sources.note: Nothing. Phonology ch. 1.2 (pp. 5-17) covers vowels, consonants, semi-vowel and 'Tons et syllabes' (pp. 14-17): two level tones H/B plus falling and rising contours, lexical and grammatical tone, tone rules, open syllables. No mention of accent/stress/intensité/proéminence anywhere in the 122 scanned pages (a full-text search for stress/accent) and none in the tone section read from the page scan.
